milestone: Native VS Code package and real editor acceptance
implementation: Bundle a thin VS Code native language-client adapter with pinned dependencies and full runtime notices, built using Bun
Associate only .k sources, provide TextMate coloring and native bracket/comment/indent rules
Launch the configured native binary directly without shell or Node transport flags; require trust, machine-scoped executable configuration and local documents
Forward one optional explicit project manifest and placement flag; restart serially for settings/workspace changes or user command
Use a log output channel, nonblocking startup error actions and disposal/restart recovery
Build a VSIX with an explicit file allowlist, excluding sources, test tools and node_modules

real_editor_checks: Packed VSIX activates for .k and starts the real native server in a multi-root window
Go to definition follows an imported function to its source
Workspace references find unopened callers and respect the selected root
Rename reaches the editor as a checked workspace edit proposal
Partly typed expression names receive native completion
Unsaved dependency edits recheck callers and clearing errors updates diagnostics
Format Document applies Unicode/CRLF edits, is idempotent and leaves disk files unchanged
Explicit project configuration restarts the native server and resolves package imports
Manual server restart restores checked editor features
unit_coverage: Native executable argv without shell parsing or injected stdio flag
Explicit manifest/placement configuration and multi-root path ambiguity
Trust gating and machine-scoped executable configuration
Serialized restarts, failed startup/disposal recovery, notification independence and shutdown
TextMate/Oniguruma keyword/type/operator/number/comment scopes and escaped/unterminated String boundaries
qualification.installed_profile: Isolated temporary profile and extension directory under ignored build/native/editor
qualification.host_loading: Installed VSIX files loaded in the real VS Code Extension Development Host

limitations: Native compiler/LLVM binaries are not bundled; server build/path setup remains required
Only installed VS Code 1.142.0 on macOS ARM64 qualified; declared minimum engine compatibility does not qualify other versions
Extension Development Host acceptance, not comprehensive manual/accessibility, Marketplace or other-editor qualification
One server and optional manifest per window; no per-folder/ancestor manifest discovery
Native semantic/backend limits, synchronous analysis and completion-recovery limitations remain unchanged
Lexical coloring only; no semantic tokens, debugger, web or qualified remote-host support
No C++ compiler/runtime/GPU implementation, JS prototype or website changes
